checks: (i) compare the spectrum table the program shows with the stated values, and note agree or not
(ii) compare the Dynamics tab's Cutoff Frequency and Number of Modes with the stated values, and note agree or not; if the window shows the file's value in another unit, note that once
(iii) write down the command that saved the imported model; whether the program let you choose the name and the folder; the name and folder the saved file took; whether the program asked anything
(iv) note what the spectrum options window (Options > Spectrum) offers for axis units and interpolation

(v) on a sacrificial duplicate: the folder samples/sample-dyn-export-trial holds sample-dyn-export-trial.mbf, a copy of the same run file as the window sample (cpb-dyn-c-n01-flat--srss-srss); in that folder only:
1. Import sample-dyn-export-trial.mbf: File > Import from the Main window, select the file and click Import. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/import_mbf.htm ("IMPORT MBF"; CAEPIPE-IMPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12]
2. From the Layout window, choose File > Export ("To export a model, select the menu command File > Export from the Layout window."). [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/export_mbf.htm (user's manual, "EXPORT MBF"; CAEPIPE-EXPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12]
3. Before touching the dialog, write down the files the folder now holds, by name.
4. In the Export Model dialog, choose "Model batch file (*.mbf)" as the Save as type. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/export_mbf.htm (user's manual, "EXPORT MBF"; CAEPIPE-EXPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12]
5. Note whether the dialog lets you set the name sample-dyn-export-trial.export.mbf and this folder, and whether it displays them before anything is written.
6. If it does, click Export; if not, click Cancel. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/export_mbf.htm (user's manual, "EXPORT MBF"; CAEPIPE-EXPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12]
7. Note the files the folder then holds, by name.
8. Nothing in samples/sample-dyn-window or in any case folder is opened or touched by this trial.
consequences: (i) not agreeing, or not made: form B (spectrum table typed) for every dynamics run

(ii) another unit: the cutoff correction applies to whichever single form of a pair is run; the owner sets the stated value only if a public page states the conversion, and otherwise skips the run and notes it
(iii) the model cannot be saved as <run id>.mod in the run's folder: every hand-entry and every dynamics run is skipped and noted

(v) the dialog did not let you set the name and the folder, or a file was written before a destination was offered: no run exports at this sitting, and the export steps of every run are skipped and noted
dry_run.sample: the dry-run sample, which carries the added records (the OPMISC dynamics options record and the SPCMS table)
dry_run.save_command: a run's model file is <run id>.mbf and its saved model <run id>.mod in the same folder, so no other name is needed; the Save page says "This command saves model data to a .mod file format." (https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/save__ctrl_s_.htm (user's manual, "Save (Ctrl+S)"), read 2026-11-13), and the File Menu page documents Save and no command for saving a model under another name (https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/file_menu_2.htm (user's manual, "File Menu"), read 2026-11-13); so the command, whether it lets the person choose the name and folder, and the name and folder the saved file takes are observed at the dry run (check iii); every instruction refers to that command

export.condition: the dry run's check (v), on its sacrificial duplicate (dry_run.export_trial)
quotes: To export a model, select the menu command File > Export from the Layout window.
The Export Model dialog is shown. Selecting the “Save as type” option as “Model batch file (*.mbf)” will export the stress model in CAEPIPE latest version.
Once done, click on Export button to write to an .mbf file.
export.runs: the five hand-entry runs and every dynamics run at strike numbers 1 to 10 (both forms of each pair and the single typed form at strike 6); no other run
export.statement: an export is a model batch file the program writes, at the owner's choice, from a run's saved model (<run id>.mod) as the program holds it after that run's instruction, including what was entered or set by hand; it is not the pack's model file. Each export is private, like every returned file. The exports are material for later interoperability work: they put on file how the program itself writes records SWBPIPE's writer does not write today. They do not demonstrate exit criterion 6's round trip in the desktop, and they do not make any family the product refuses become supported. Nothing of SWBPIPE's reads an export in this change

hand_entry.files: each run is its own case under its run id: the person imports <run_id>.mbf, enters the one member, saves it as <run_id>.mod before analysing by the command noted at the dry run, never over the .mbf, and prints to file as <run_id>.print.csv; nothing of SWBPIPE's reads the saved file
hand_entry.held: captured at the sitting and HELD, stored sealed, until SWBPIPE's own result for this case and this load case is published by the product as checks passed; no comparison is formed before then

held_until_series.cpb-h-01: captured at the sitting and HELD, stored sealed, and not compared, until an independently justified one-parameter series supplying the evidence REQ-019 requires for the input constant_support_load, which no series does yet, as well as SWBPIPE's own result for this case and this load case published by the product as checks passed and the capture's binding to the model actually run; the series's load values are never fitted to the captured result

left_out.case: a limit stop whose gap closes under thermal growth, with a gap greater than zero
left_out.why: the page states the limits as gaps measured from the undeflected node and their sign convention, but not the unit the window takes them in for an SI model (its examples are in inches); the one-way stop (cpb-n-01) is kept, since zero needs no unit

left_out.field: Friction coefficient (stated, unitless); the load path
left_out.why: the friction coefficient is stated and needs no unit, but the case needs the target program's thermal-case option (thermal as operating minus sustained, or solved alone; https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm states both and not which is set by default for an imported file) and a SWBPIPE state with a stated normal reaction to compare with; left for a later change

left_out.field: User Hanger: Spring Rate, Hanger Load
left_out.why: the page states the fields but not the unit the window takes them in for an SI model (its examples are in lb/in and lb); the designed Hanger type selects from a manufacturer's catalogue, which is not invented data (https://docs.sstcae.com/tech_manual/hanger.htm)

left_out.page: none: no saved public page documents the wind load window
left_out.why: no field is stated, so wind_pressure_relation cannot be carried by an instruction

left_out.field: Number of Thermal Loads, and T2 under Misc > Loads
left_out.why: two changes, not one (the number of thermal loads and the second temperature), and the page does not state the unit the window takes T2 in

hand_entry.one_way_cases: a one-way support: its capture is taken at the sitting and held; whether SWBPIPE's result for it may be compared is read from the product at each solve and is recorded nowhere here.
hand_entry.rule: the tracked document's model is the WRITTEN BASE; the case's SWBPIPE model is the base with the member's support records appended (benchmark_hand_entry.hand_entry_model); no support or load record is added to a written file
hand_entry.skip: If the window does not offer a field as the page describes it, skip this case and note it on the run line; do not enter an equivalent.

The reviewer who raised it had seen no result. Which class these cases are compared under is decided by the owner at their review of the benchmark record; until then each is reported under both, and no agreement count is stated for them under the named class alone.

runs.label: srss-srss
runs.screening_waits_for: a headless modal and response-spectrum entry of the product, which main does not have; until then the capture is held

window_instruction.text:
1. Use this run only if the dry run's check of the dry-run sample that carries the same spectrum table agreed (the owner compared the table the program showed with the stated values and noted agreement on that sample's run line); otherwise run its counterpart cpb-dyn-c-n08-flat--srss-srss-table-typed instead.
2. Import cpb-dyn-c-n08-flat--srss-srss.mbf: File > Import from the Main window, select the file and click Import; it is the model file with the OPMISC and SPCMS records added. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/import_mbf.htm, section "Format of .MBF" (CAEPIPE-IMPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12]
3. Select Spectrums from the Misc menu. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]
4. If the List window for spectrums shows a spectrum named DYNFLAT with these 2 pairs of values, 0.125 Hz, 2500 mm/sec2; 1000 Hz, 2500 mm/sec2, go on; otherwise skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]
5. If Options > Spectrum, which sets the units of the X- and Y-axes and the interpolation method, shows the X-axis unit Frequency (Hz), the Y-axis unit Acceleration (mm/sec2) and a linear interpolation method, go on; otherwise skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]
6. Under the menu Loads > Spectrum, type a Level Tag L1 ("Type an alpha-numeric name (up to 8 characters long) in this field."). The MBF has no documented record for the spectrum assignment, so it is entered here; the file's OPMISC record also states the two sums. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/load_cases.htm (user's manual, "Load cases"), read 2026-11-12; https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
7. Double-click the row ("Double click on the row to assign the spectrum load."). [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
8. X, Y and Z spectrums ("Select a spectrum from the drop-down combo box, which should have been input in the spectrum table for each global direction."): Y: DYNFLAT, Factor 1; Z: DYNFLAT, Factor 1; and no spectrum for X (if the window requires a spectrum for every direction, skip this run and note it). [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
9. Factor ("The multiplying (scale) factor for the spectrum is input here.") is a pure multiplier of the spectrum's ordinates, with no unit. If the window offers one Factor per direction, enter each as the previous step states it. If the window offers a single Factor and this run states the same factor for every direction it loads, enter that value; if it states different factors for different directions, skip this run and note it. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
10. Mode Sum ("Pick one of three choices, SRSS (square root of sum of squares), Closely spaced or Absolute."): SRSS. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
11. Direction Sum ("Pick one of two choices, SRSS (square root of the sum of squares) or Absolute."): SRSS. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
12. Before the analysis, open Options > Analysis, tab Dynamics. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
13. Check that Cutoff Frequency reads 900 Hz and Number of Modes 6; a value that differs is set to the stated value by hand and noted on the run line. The vendor's public import page states the file's cutoff frequency value with no unit; Hertz is taken from the analysis page's description of the window's Cutoff Frequency field. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/import_mbf.htm, section "Format of .MBF" (CAEPIPE-IMPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12]
3. Options > Spectrum sets the units of the X- and Y-axes and the interpolation method: if it offers Frequency (Hz) for the X-axis and Acceleration (mm/sec2) for the Y-axis (the units the same page names for a spectrum) and a linear interpolation method (spectra are interpolated linearly or logarithmically), set them; otherwise skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12; https://docs.sstcae.com/tech_manual/dynamic_analysis.htm (technical reference, "Dynamic analysis", section "Response Spectrum"), read 2026-11-12]
4. Select Spectrums from the Misc menu. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]
5. In the List window for spectrums, type a spectrum named DYNFLAT in the Name column with 2 pairs of values, each a frequency in Hz then an acceleration in mm/sec2: 0.125, 2500; 1000, 2500. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]

11. Direction Sum ("Pick one of two choices, SRSS (square root of the sum of squares) or Absolute."): SRSS. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
12. Before the analysis, open Options > Analysis, tab Dynamics. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
13. Check that Cutoff Frequency reads 900 Hz and Number of Modes 5; a value that differs is set to the stated value by hand and noted on the run line. 14. Check that Include Missing Mass Correction is unchecked. If the tab does not show one of these fields, skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
15. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
16. Loads > Load Cases: check the box next to Response Spectrum for analysis. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/load_cases.htm (user's manual, "Load cases"), read 2026-11-12]
17. Save the model as cpb-dyn-c-n02-flat--abs-srss-table-typed.mod in this folder by the command you noted at the dry run. Do not save over the imported file. If the program will not save under that name, skip this run and note it.

20. If the window does not offer a field as the page describes it, skip this case and note it on the run line; do not enter an equivalent.

5. If Options > Spectrum, which sets the units of the X- and Y-axes and the interpolation method, shows the X-axis unit Frequency (Hz), the Y-axis unit Acceleration (mm/sec2) and a linear interpolation method, go on; otherwise skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]

8. X, Y and Z spectrums ("Select a spectrum from the drop-down combo box, which should have been input in the spectrum table for each global direction."): Y: DYNFLAT, Factor 1; Z: DYNFLAT, Factor 1; and no spectrum for X (if the window requires a spectrum for every direction, skip this run and note it). 15. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
16. Loads > Load Cases: check the box next to Response Spectrum for analysis. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/load_cases.htm (user's manual, "Load cases"), read 2026-11-12]
17. Save the model as cpb-dyn-c-n02-flat--nrl-abs.mod in this folder by the command you noted at the dry run. Do not save over the imported file. If the program will not save under that name, skip this run and note it.

[https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analyze__f12_.htm (user's manual, "Analyze (F12)"), read 2026-11-13]
19. Then print the results to file: in the Results window, File > Print (Ctrl+P), click All, then To File, and save the .csv file as cpb-dyn-c-n02-flat--nrl-abs.print.csv. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/print__ctrl_p__2.htm (user's manual, "Print (Ctrl+P)"), read 2026-11-12]

[https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/load_cases.htm (user's manual, "Load cases"), read 2026-11-12; https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
7. Double-click the row ("Double click on the row to assign the spectrum load."). [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
8. X, Y and Z spectrums ("Select a spectrum from the drop-down combo box, which should have been input in the spectrum table for each global direction."): Y: DYNFLAT, Factor 1; Z: DYNFLAT, Factor 1; and no spectrum for X (if the window requires a spectrum for every direction, skip this run and note it). [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]

12. Before the analysis, open Options > Analysis, tab Dynamics. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
13. Check that Cutoff Frequency reads 900 Hz and Number of Modes 6; a value that differs is set to the stated value by hand and noted on the run line. The vendor's public import page states the file's cutoff frequency value with no unit; Hertz is taken from the analysis page's description of the window's Cutoff Frequency field. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/import_mbf.htm, section "Format of .MBF" (CAEPIPE-IMPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12; https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
14. Check that Include Missing Mass Correction is unchecked. If the tab does not show one of these fields, skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
15. Before the analysis, check the gravity the window shows against this run's request ("Gravitational Acceleration and Direction"): Vertical Direction Y; Gravitational Acceleration 9.80665 m/sec2; Direction of Gravity downward along Y (-Y). The page says to "click the “Change” button to modify the Gravitational Acceleration and the corresponding Direction of Gravity"; change nothing. If the window shows another value or direction, or does not show them, skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]

17. Save the model as cpb-dyn-c-n16-flat--nrl-abs-table-typed.mod in this folder by the command you noted at the dry run. Do not save over the imported file. If the program will not save under that name, skip this run and note it.
18. Then analyze the model by File > Analyze (F12); the page says: "At the end of analysis, you are asked whether you want to “View results?” Click on OK to see results or Cancel to return to the main window." [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analyze__f12_.htm (user's manual, "Analyze (F12)"), read 2026-11-13]
19. Then print the results to file: in the Results window, File > Print (Ctrl+P), click All, then To File, and save the .csv file as cpb-dyn-c-n16-flat--nrl-abs-table-typed.print.csv. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/print__ctrl_p__2.htm (user's manual, "Print (Ctrl+P)"), read 2026-11-12]
20. If the window does not offer a field as the page describes it, skip this case and note it on the run line; do not enter an equivalent.
A further run of the same model in one session is not open for this run: the window's Mode Sum lists no NRL; import this run's file. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]

runs.screening_waits_for: a headless modal and response-spectrum entry of the product, which main does not have; until then the capture is held

window_instruction.text:
1. Use this run if the dry run's check of the dry-run sample that carries the same spectrum table did not agree or was not made; otherwise run its counterpart cpb-dyn-d-n08-flat--closely-spaced-srss instead.
2. Import cpb-dyn-d-n08-flat--closely-spaced-srss-table-typed.mbf: File > Import from the Main window, select the file and click Import; it is the model file with the OPMISC record added and no spectrum table. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/import_mbf.htm, section "Format of .MBF" (CAEPIPE-IMPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12]
3. Options > Spectrum sets the units of the X- and Y-axes and the interpolation method: if it offers Frequency (Hz) for the X-axis and Acceleration (mm/sec2) for the Y-axis (the units the same page names for a spectrum) and a linear interpolation method (spectra are interpolated linearly or logarithmically), set them; otherwise skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12; https://docs.sstcae.com/tech_manual/dynamic_analysis.htm (technical reference, "Dynamic analysis", section "Response Spectrum"), read 2026-11-12]
4. Select Spectrums from the Misc menu. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]
5. In the List window for spectrums, type a spectrum named DYNFLAT in the Name column with 2 pairs of values, each a frequency in Hz then an acceleration in mm/sec2: 0.125, 2500; 1000, 2500. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrums.htm (user's manual, "Spectrums"), read 2026-11-12]
6. Under the menu Loads > Spectrum, type a Level Tag L1 ("Type an alpha-numeric name (up to 8 characters long) in this field."). The MBF has no documented record for the spectrum assignment, so it is entered here; the file's OPMISC record also states the two sums. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/load_cases.htm (user's manual, "Load cases"), read 2026-11-12; https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
7. Double-click the row ("Double click on the row to assign the spectrum load."). [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
8. X, Y and Z spectrums ("Select a spectrum from the drop-down combo box, which should have been input in the spectrum table for each global direction."): Y: DYNFLAT, Factor 1; and no spectrum for X, Z (if the window requires a spectrum for every direction, skip this run and note it). [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
9. Factor ("The multiplying (scale) factor for the spectrum is input here.") is a pure multiplier of the spectrum's ordinates, with no unit. If the window offers one Factor per direction, enter each as the previous step states it. If the window offers a single Factor and this run states the same factor for every direction it loads, enter that value; if it states different factors for different directions, skip this run and note it. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
10. Mode Sum ("Pick one of three choices, SRSS (square root of sum of squares), Closely spaced or Absolute."): Closely spaced. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
11. Direction Sum ("Pick one of two choices, SRSS (square root of the sum of squares) or Absolute."): SRSS. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]
12. Before the analysis, open Options > Analysis, tab Dynamics. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
13. Check that Cutoff Frequency reads 900 Hz and Number of Modes 6; a value that differs is set to the stated value by hand and noted on the run line. The vendor's public import page states the file's cutoff frequency value with no unit; Hertz is taken from the analysis page's description of the window's Cutoff Frequency field. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/import_mbf.htm, section "Format of .MBF" (CAEPIPE-IMPORT-MBF, execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-01/Source_Basis_Register.md), read 2026-11-12; https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
14. Check that Include Missing Mass Correction is unchecked. If the tab does not show one of these fields, skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
15. Before the analysis, check the gravity the window shows against this run's request ("Gravitational Acceleration and Direction"): Vertical Direction Y; Gravitational Acceleration 9.80665 m/sec2; Direction of Gravity downward along Y (-Y). The page says to "click the “Change” button to modify the Gravitational Acceleration and the corresponding Direction of Gravity"; change nothing. If the window shows another value or direction, or does not show them, skip this run and note it on the run line. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analysis.htm (user's manual, "Analysis"), read 2026-11-12]
16. Loads > Load Cases: check the box next to Response Spectrum for analysis. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/load_cases.htm (user's manual, "Load cases"), read 2026-11-12]
17. Save the model as cpb-dyn-d-n08-flat--closely-spaced-srss-table-typed.mod in this folder by the command you noted at the dry run. Do not save over the imported file. If the program will not save under that name, skip this run and note it.
18. Then analyze the model by File > Analyze (F12); the page says: "At the end of analysis, you are asked whether you want to “View results?” Click on OK to see results or Cancel to return to the main window." [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/analyze__f12_.htm (user's manual, "Analyze (F12)"), read 2026-11-13]
19. Then print the results to file: in the Results window, File > Print (Ctrl+P), click All, then To File, and save the .csv file as cpb-dyn-d-n08-flat--closely-spaced-srss-table-typed.print.csv. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/print__ctrl_p__2.htm (user's manual, "Print (Ctrl+P)"), read 2026-11-12]
20. If the window does not offer a field as the page describes it, skip this case and note it on the run line; do not enter an equivalent.
Only if the command you noted at the dry run lets you choose the saved file's name and folder: instead of importing this run's file, you MAY, with the model of this case's comparable run (cpb-dyn-d-n08-flat--srss-srss-table-typed) still open, change Mode Sum to Closely spaced and Direction Sum to SRSS in Loads > Spectrum, save the model as cpb-dyn-d-n08-flat--closely-spaced-srss-table-typed.mod in this run's folder by the command you noted at the dry run, analyze it by File > Analyze (F12), print the results to file as cpb-dyn-d-n08-flat--closely-spaced-srss-table-typed.print.csv, and write on this run's run line that the setting was made by hand. Importing this run's file remains the default. [https://docs.sstcae.com/users_manual/spectrum_load.htm (user's manual, "Spectrum Load"), read 2026-11-13]

option_addition.closely_spaced: the technical reference states that the closely spaced method is the ten percent method of NRC Guide 1.92 (DYNAMICS_PAGE); SWBPIPE's ten_percent rule corresponds only where it is the same rule
conditions: (a) every added record is one the vendor's public import page documents (OPMISC, SPCMS); any other is refused
(b) whole records only, recorded line by line with the resulting file's hash; the resulting file is not the bound file and is never imported as one
(c) no node, element, support or load record changes: removing the added lines gives the writer's file byte for byte

(d) what no documented record carries is done in the program's window by the person, as each run's window_instruction says: the assignment of a spectrum to directions with its factors and the two sums are entered (Spectrum Load page); the gravitational acceleration and direction are checked, not entered; the response-spectrum analysis is selected (Load cases page)
option_addition.depends_on: relies on REQ-005 as placed in execution/PKG-17/DEL-17-05/ScopeOfWork.md, which admits a declared addition of whole documented options records; these runs remain capture-only pending the run-record and comparison work that scope's Not met block names
option_addition.files: each run is its own case under its run id: the person imports <run_id>.mbf, saves it as <run_id>.mod before analysing by the command noted at the dry run, and prints to file as <run_id>.print.csv
option_addition.nrl: Series dynamics-nrl-abs and dynamics-nrl-srss, and their -table-typed twins, declare Mode Sum code 4, NRL, which the import page documents for the OPMISC record; the Spectrum Load page lists only three choices for the window's Mode Sum (SRSS, Closely spaced, Absolute). Those runs keep the file's documented code; their instruction reads: Continue only if the displayed Mode Sum is NRL; otherwise record what it shows and skip.
option_addition.opmisc_cutoff_unit: the import page gives OPMISC's cutoff frequency without a unit; the analysis page states the window's Cutoff Frequency in Hertz (tab "Dynamics"), so the record's value is read as Hz, an inference each run's window check confirms before the analysis; every other OPMISC field's values are stated on the import page
opmisc_fields: include friction in dynamics: 0 off, 1 on
spectrum mode sum: 1 absolute, 2 SRSS, 3 closely spaced, 4 NRL
option_addition.opmisc_omitted: the tenth field, gravitational direction (valid from version 15.10), is not written: the public page names it but does not state its values; the person checks the Direction of Gravity in the window before the analysis
option_addition.pairs: each dynamics run but one case's is declared in two forms with different files: form A (series without suffix) adds the options record and the spectrum table; form B (series ending -table-typed) adds the options record alone and the person types the spectrum table. Exactly one of a pair is run at the sitting: form A only if the dry run's check of the dry-run sample that carries the same spectrum table agreed, form B otherwise. The pair is never both screened
option_addition.same_session_alternative: offered as an instruction only: every run that is a further combination of a model whose comparable run comes earlier in the strike order ends with a paragraph letting the owner, only if the command noted at the dry run lets the owner choose the saved file's name and folder, and with that comparable run's model still open, change Mode Sum and Direction Sum in Loads > Spectrum (the Spectrum Load page names both) instead of importing the run's file; per-file import remains the default and is what the pack is checked against. For an NRL run the paragraph says the alternative is not open, because the window's Mode Sum lists no NRL
option_addition.single_form: cpb-dyn-c-n08-two is declared in the typed form only (series dynamics-comparable-table-typed, run cpb-dyn-c-n08-two--srss-srss-table-typed). Its spectrum table (DYNTWO, three rows) is carried by no dry-run sample, so the condition on which the form that writes the table may be run could never be met; by design the typed form is this case's only form. It is not a run that was skipped
option_addition.spcms_codes: the page states the SPCMS fields but not their codes; the codes used, abscissa and ordinate interpolation 0 = linear, abscissa units 0 = frequency (Hz), ordinate units 3 = acceleration (mm/sec2), are those the same page states for the fields of the same names in the SPLVL record, and the spectrums page states for a spectrum text file's units; that they hold for SPCMS is an inference, so each run's window entries ask the person to check the table as the window shows it
option_addition.spcms_fields: first line: name (up to 32 characters), number of entries, abscissa interpolation, ordinate interpolation, abscissa units, ordinate units; then one line per entry: name, abscissa, ordinate
option_addition.strike_order: every dynamics run carries strike_order, one integer across the part, 1 first; both forms of a pair share it: the ten comparable runs by case rank, then the further combinations of ranks 1 to 3, then the diagonal case's three further mode sums

pressure_hypothesis.refuted_by: on the closed straights P1 and P2, the target program's change between the pressure-default and pressure-elongation-on runs differs, beyond the screening profile, from the closed forms' change: each anchor's axial reaction changing by (1 - 2 nu) p A_i (P1), or the free end's axial displacement changing by (1 - 2 nu) p A_i L/(E A_s) (P2); or its axial results there do not change at all
pressure_hypothesis.statement: HYPOTHESIS, which the pressure-elongation-on series tests and does not assume: the target program's Bourdon effect switch, with Bourdon in the sustained load cases, corresponds on straight pipe to SWBPIPE's pressure elongation, the closed-end free pressure strain (1 - 2 nu) p A_i/(E A_s), applied in case:sustained. rigid_support_override.rule: a model names rigid_support_stiffness on every load case its thermal loads enter (the thermal case and the operating sum) when it has two or more anchors, each of which restrains the pipe's axial growth; a model with one anchor (a free thermal cantilever) is not relabelled. rigid_support_override.text: The class was changed on 13 November 2026 after first-tranche screens of 28 October and 12 November 2026, on grounds independent of any result: the vendor's public anchor page states a finite default stiffness, and textbook mechanics predicts its effect (series S3). The reviewer who raised it had seen no result. Which class these cases are compared under is decided by the owner at their review of the benchmark record; until then each is reported under both, and no agreement count is stated for them under the named class alone.

pressure-bend-opening.description: the closed cantilever L of P7 in its pressure-default and pressure-elongation-on runs. It measures any additional in-plane angular response of the free end associated with the target program's Bourdon switch, with its bend pressure correction field held off. Under the stated linear model, uniform free axial strain is excluded as an explanation of a rotation change (build_p7), so SWBPIPE's change of that rotation between the runs is 0. HYPOTHESIS: the target program's change, if any, is bend opening by its switch. The series cannot by itself identify that program's internal formula, establish a general law of bend opening, or exclude every undocumented effect of the switch. The same pair of an anchored L (P4) does not serve: between anchors the legs' elongation bends the L and turns its ends too

rigid-support-length.description: HYPOTHESIS, which the series can refute: a program whose rigid anchor is the stated finite stiffness shows the expansion axial force reduced by the predicted factor 1/(1 + 2 E A/(k_t L)) and the sustained end moment by 1/(1 + 2 E I/(k_r L)); one with ideal anchors shows neither. The lengths take the axial reduction from about 5e-4, clearly above the exact class's 1e-4, down to about 6e-6, negligible. DECLARED BEFORE ANY RUN: a later SWBPIPE side that states the vendor's stiffness explicitly, as springs, may change a row's numerical standing, because a very stiff finite support worsens the system's conditioning; that would be reported as its own finding with the stiffness named, and it would say nothing about agreement. That side is not built. This series is also the convention series for triage of anchored cases in tranches 1 and 2, whose files cannot name this input without changing their bytes.

shear-thick-wall.description: S1 complements the tranche 1 series shear-dt (OD 219.1 mm, span 3 m, L/OD 13.7, D/t 10 to 100, weight, tip force and thermal): S1 takes the thick-wall end (D/t 4 to 20) at L/OD 3.7 with a tip force that dominates the weight, so the shear term is several percent of the deflection and the dependence of the shear coefficient on the wall ratio is resolved well above the printed resolution; shear-dt measures the same input where it is near the named-inexact tolerance. HYPOTHESIS, which the series can refute: a program whose beams carry transverse shear with a hollow-circle coefficient shows each member's tip deflection larger than the Euler-Bernoulli value by about the predicted relative difference; one without shear shows none. The predicted fraction grows as the wall thins at this diameter (module text).
